A watch folder that renames new downloads into your library as soon as they finish, missing subtitles downloaded after every rename, and a Plex scan right after renaming so new files show up in seconds. Turning on any of them starts a free {{ trial_days }}-day trial.

q: Will Windows warn me when I install it?
a: It can. Windows SmartScreen shows Windows protected your PC for apps from new publishers that don't have a paid code-signing certificate yet. Click More info, then Run anyway. The installer is built by GitHub from the public source code.

q: Does it work with Jellyfin or Emby?
a: The names PathRenamer writes follow Plex's conventions (Movie (Year) folders, S01E01 episodes, .eng.srt subtitles), which Jellyfin and Emby read too. The automatic library scan works with Plex only for now.
Yes. Undo Last puts the last batch back, and Edit → Rename History can undo older renames, even after closing the app. Subtitles PathRenamer downloaded for a rename are removed with it.

q: Can I keep seeding torrents after renaming?
a: Yes. Set Settings → Options → When renaming to Hard-link the files. Your library gets the new names while the torrent keeps its files, without using extra space. See Rename for Plex and keep seeding.

Yes: fansub names like [Group] Show - 12 (1080p).mkv, absolute episode numbers, and titles looked up on TVmaze and AniDB. You choose season numbers (S01E12) or absolute numbers in the format settings.

q: What happens to subtitles in a Subs folder?
a: They are found and renamed with their video, with the language Plex expects: Movie (2021).eng.srt, Movie (2021).spa.srt, and .forced or .sdh where the name says so.

No. It reads file names, and the start and end of a file to tell its resolution and codecs. Titles are looked up on TVmaze, Cinemeta and AniDB (and TMDB if you add a key). When you download subtitles, OpenSubtitles gets the file's fingerprint and title. There are no ads and no tracking. Details: Privacy.

q: Is there a Mac or Linux version?
a: Not yet. PathRenamer runs on Windows 10 and 11.
In %APPDATA%\PathRenamer: config.json (settings), history.json (rename history, for undo) and a log file. Your Plex token and OpenSubtitles password are stored encrypted for your Windows account.

q: How do I report a bug or ask for a feature?
a: Open an issue on GitHub. Include the file name that went wrong and what you expected; the log file in %APPDATA%\PathRenamer helps too.
